A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PROREASON research and contain readable main text, tables, figures, and appendices A.1–A.7. Content can be matched reliably across page shifts, figure reordering, and table renumbering.

before.justification: Sections 4 and A.5 report original benchmark evaluations, downstream model training results, efficiency measurements, and ablation studies.

after.justification: V4 retains those original empirical results and adds the maximum-loop-iteration experiment in Section A.5.8 and Table 14.

M1.justification: The five-agent framework, Memory component, perception/reasoning workflow, restart procedure, and downstream distillation remain unchanged. The new iteration sweep evaluates the existing method; reordered prompt figures retain their prompt contents.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MME, MMMU, MathVista, HallusionBench, MathVerse, MMStar, and A-OKVQA with the same task coverage. The new iteration experiment reuses MME, MMMU, and MathVista without introducing another dataset or test scenario.

E2.justification: Direct, VDGD, CCoT, CoT, and ReAct remain the framework comparators, and R1-Onevision-7B remains the downstream model comparator. New Table 14 reuses the existing framework comparator set and scores. MiMo-VL is cited but not evaluated.

E3.justification: Section A.5.8 adds a controlled evaluation of GPT-4o-mini-powered PROREASON with maximum loop iterations of 1–5 on three retained datasets. Existing settings remain unchanged, including the distinct 1/3/5 attempt-allowance experiment in Section A.5.5.

E4.justification: V4 adds sensitivity analysis asking how the maximum number of perception iterations affects performance and when gains diminish. Earlier sub-agent ablations, attempt-allowance tests, reasoning assessments, expert-frequency analyses, and demonstrative cases are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests for these results. The new iteration study follows the existing practice of reporting point estimates without uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Previously reported numerical results are unchanged. New Table 14 adds results for loop limits 1–4; at limit 1, scores are 90.8 on MME, 59.2 on MMMU, and 52.3 on MathVista. Limit 5 repeats the existing 91.9, 61.6, and 54.9 scores. These are additional settings, not improved same-setting results.

T1.justification: Section 3's formal description and notation are retained. No mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or substantively revised; the new iteration analysis is empirical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the contributions of decoupled perception and reasoning, LLM assistance, and downstream distillation, including the average performance-gain claim reaching 13.2%. The additional appendix evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Section A.5.8 newly interprets the relatively small changes beyond three iterations as indicating that most questions need at most three cycles, while harder questions benefit from further perception. This extends the adaptive-iteration explanation; existing cumulative-error and agent-collaboration limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V4 adds an explicit code-availability statement and repository link in the abstract. Both versions retain Section 7's future-release promise, and actual repository availability cannot be verified from the PDFs. Existing implementation settings and prompt contents are retained.

R1.justification: V4 adds the MiMo-VL technical report, cited as Xiaomi and Team (2025), to the introduction and references. The remaining related-work discussion and positioning relative to earlier reasoning frameworks are unchanged.

P1.justification: Limited structural edits add Section A.5.8 and acknowledgements, update Jingwei Dong's affiliation and email, and adjust cross-references. Existing scientific prose and the overall narrative organization remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: V4 adds Table 14, renumbers the existing configuration table as Table 15, and reflows the appendix. It also reorders the two-agent and five-agent prompt figures and corrects their mismatched captions in Figures 13 and 15. Their underlying prompt contents are unchanged.

improvement.justification: Compared with v3's attempt-allowance and average-iteration analyses, v4 directly examines maximum-loop sensitivity in Table 14. This additional evidence, corrected prompt-caption associations, and added code-access information modestly improve transparency and usability. The absence of uncertainty estimates and unverified repository availability limit the gains; the core method and earlier results remain unchanged.
